Michael Gorzynski (40%) | stadium = [[Polish Army Stadium]] | season = [[2025–26 Ekstraklasa|2025–26]] | position = Ekstraklasa, 6th of 18 | website = {{URL|https://legia.com/}} | pattern_la1 = _legia2627h | pattern_b1 = _legia2627h | pattern_ra1 = _legia2627h | pattern_sh1 = _legia2627h | pattern_so1 = | leftarm1 = FFFFFF | body1 = FFFFFF | rightarm1 = FFFFFF | shorts1 = 000000 | socks1 = 000000 | pattern_la2 = _legia2627a | pattern_b2 = _legia2627a | pattern_ra2 = _legia2627a | pattern_sh2 = _legia2627a | pattern_so2 = _adidaswhitel | leftarm2 = 00842c | body2 = 00842c | rightarm2 = 00842c | shorts2 = | socks2 = 00842c | pattern_la3 = | pattern_b3 = | pattern_ra3 = | pattern_sh3 = | pattern_so3 = | leftarm3 = | body3 = | rightarm3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = }} {{Legia Warsaw sections}} '''Legia Warszawa''' ({{IPA|pl|ˈlɛɡʲja varˈʂava|lang|Pl-Legia Warszawa.ogg}}), commonly referred to as '''Legia Warsaw''' or simply '''Legia''', is a professional [[football club (association football)|football club]] based in [[Warsaw]], Poland. Legia is the most successful Polish football club in history, winning a record 15 {{Lang|pl|[[Ekstraklasa]]|italic=no}} champions titles, a record 21 [[Polish Cup]] and 6 [[Polish Super Cup]] trophies. The club's home venue is the [[Polish Army Stadium]] (''Stadion Wojska Polskiego''). Legia is the only Polish club never to have been relegated from the top flight of Polish football since [[World War II]] (see: [[1936 Legia Warsaw season]]).{{Cite web|url=https://legia.com/o-klubie|title=O klubie|website=Legia Warsaw|language=pl|access-date=8 May 2021|archive-date=29 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210429093529/https://legia.com/o-klubie|url-status=live}} Legia was formed between 5 and 15 March 1916 during military operations in [[World War I]], as the main football club of the [[Polish Legions in World War I|Polish Legions]]. After the war, the club was reactivated on 14 March 1920 in an officer casino in Warsaw as Wojskowy Klub Sportowy Warszawa, renamed Legia in 1923 after merger with another local club, Korona. It became the main official football club of the [[Polish Army]] – '''''Wojskowy Klub Sportowy Legia Warszawa''''' ({{Literal translation|Military Sports Club Legia Warsaw}}). From 1949 to 1957, Legia was known as '''''CWKS Warszawa''''' ({{Literal translation|Central Military Sports Club Warsaw}}) Before 8 April 2004, it was owned by [[Pol-Mot]] and from 8 April 2004 (sold for 3 million [[Polish zloty|zlotys]]) until 9 January 2014, it was owned by media conglomerate [[ITI Group]].{{cite web|url=http://ekstraklasa.wp.pl/kat,32284,title,Oficjalnie-ITI-sprzedalo-Legie,wid,16312159,wiadomosc.html|title=Lotto Ekstraklasa – Piłka nożna – WP SportoweFakty|work=Ekstraklasa |access-date=9 January 2014|archive-date=14 February 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140214060047/http://ekstraklasa.wp.pl/kat,32284,title,Oficjalnie-ITI-sprzedalo-Legie,wid,16312159,wiadomosc.html|url-status=live}} The club is currently owned by Dariusz Mioduski who serves as the club's chairman."}}
